storytellers.name: Pearl Cooley
facts: Diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at two months old
Early challenges with growth, digestion and severe lung disease
Required daily treatments, medications and chest physiotherapy
First double lung transplant at age 18
Second double lung transplant two years later
Lung function has since declined despite years of stability
Campaigning for Trikafta access, which remains out of reach for some transplant recipients
Works as an athletic trainer for hockey teams across the GTA
Also works as a part-time medical assistant

quotes.text: We cannot forget the people who are living with CF today. We need to support current patients, improve access to life-changing medications, and ensure earlier diagnosis.
A lung transplant is not a cure. It is a life-saving treatment.
quotes.note: Paraphrased by the org as 'as Pearl reminds us...' — confirm exact wording with her.

storytellers.name: Sandra Markus
facts: Son Zach born with developmental differences 25 years ago
Took 18 years to receive a diagnosis
Diagnosed with a CHD2-related disorder at age 18
Condition can include epilepsy, autism, intellectual disability and developmental delays
Support system disappeared on transition to adult care
A dermatological treatment triggered a severe, persisting psychiatric reaction
Now experiences memory loss and cognitive decline resembling dementia

quotes.text: In Ontario, that meant no diagnosis, no meaningful support.
We finally had answers. But the diagnosis didn't unlock care.
No coordinated team. No roadmap. No one accountable.
No specialist pathway. No integrated care. No guidance. Just silence.
Because rare does not mean invisible. Ontario can do better. And for families like ours, it must.

storytellers.note: Her entire caption is first-person — the richest single source on the account.

storytellers.name: Kristen Hummel
facts: In her early 40s attributed constantly feeling hot to perimenopause
Bloodwork instead revealed a myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN)
Condition later progressed to myelofibrosis, which scars the bone marrow
There is no cure
Volunteers with the Canadian MPN Network on awareness and access to care
storytellers.warning: No direct quote from Kristen exists in the caption. The site currently uses the org's line 'Rare disease journeys are often lifelong, but no one should have to navigate them alone' as her pull-quote — those are NOT her words. Replace with a real quote.
